disposition: Support non-promotion; exact legislative mechanism and legal-category mismatch remain unestablished.
independent_read_extent: Read the full one-page original MIBRAG statement.
Read original Commission SA.42955 paragraphs 45–54, including the complete paragraph 48 classification and adjoining regional-congestion explanation.
Read the entire current official EnWG section 13d and NetzResV section 7 from the archived original HTML, decoded as ISO-8859-1.
Read the energy source registry and its precise access/version limits. Did not independently read the 197-page StromVKG draft or certify its exhaustive relevance.
reasoning: The explicit Netzreserve terminology followed by strategic-reserve provisions raises a legitimate legal-category question. It is not an affirmative contradiction: the Commission previously expressly classified Germany’s network reserve as a capacity mechanism in strategic-reserve form while acknowledging its regional congestion function. A proposed price-capping redesign may alter classification. The domestic statute also expressly allows a network-reserve installation to take part in capacity-reserve procurement under separate conditions, while the current regulation confines ordinary network-reserve use to outside the market. These details defeat a finding based on terminology alone.
strongest_alternative: The author may be evaluating a proposed compensated strategic-capacity mechanism, or domestic/state-aid outside-market constraints may independently support its opposition.
limits: The 2016 state-aid approval predates the 2019 Regulation and expired in 2020; it cannot establish current authorisation or bind interpretation of the later definition. Current statutes were retrieved on 25 October, without an independently authenticated 19 October snapshot. Neither the legality nor the market effects of a specific return proposal were determined. Missing draft is a scope/version gate, not proof of error. No new quotation, issue record, severity or direction classification added.
